questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.

wrongReasons.mustn't: 'mustn't' means something is forbidden. Seeing a doctor is not forbidden: it is good advice.
wrongReasons.can: 'can' expresses ability or permission, not advice.
wrongReasons.would: 'would' is used for imaginary situations, not for giving advice like this.

questions.text: You ___ see a doctor. You look ill.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.

wrongReasons.although: 'although' shows a contrast. Here the rain is the reason for staying at home, so we need 'because'.
wrongReasons.so: 'so' introduces a result: 'It was raining, so I stayed at home'. Here the rain is the reason, so we use 'because'.
wrongReasons.but: 'but' adds a contrast. The rain is the reason for staying at home, not a contrast.

questions.text: I stayed at home ___ it was raining.
